advances: The credit is for one clamped vertex in the stated shell. Exactness for arbitrary extra shapes requires a common anchor.

proof:
Take a nonvertical through-cap at $(q,g)$ with unit continuous normal $u$ and base coefficient $\beta$. Put $B=u\cdot g$ and $\ell=\min_T u\cdot x$, and let $f(u),R(u)$ be the ordinary and reflected tail fractions of fact 53fe12b742a7608d. If this one cap captures all owned extra mass, the sum of the own simplex and the extra captures is at least $\Gamma_d V+E_q$. Otherwise some owned extra fiber has threshold $B-\beta\cdot(p-q)>\ell$. The opposite base $2q-p$ is a distinct binary vertex and its threshold is strictly below $2B-\ell$. The own and opposite simplex traces therefore have total mass at least $V[f(u)+R(u)]\ge V(\Gamma_d+\rho_d)$. Other fibers have nonnegative mass. Thus the same cap satisfies the lower bound in both cases. A vertical through-cap includes the own simplex, and $1>\Gamma_d+\rho_d$ since $\rho_d<\Gamma_d<1/2$. The strict upper bound on $\Gamma_d$ follows from $(1+1/d)^d>2$ for $d\ge2$ by the binomial expansion. Parallel tightening reduces the mass of any containing halfspace.

For the exact construction flip the integer coordinates at which $q_i=1$, so that $q=0$ and the added bases are in $\lbrace-1,0\rbrace^n\setminus\lbrace0\rbrace$. Every integer point of the base hull outside the binary cube has a coordinate $-1$. A convex representation then uses only added bases having that coordinate $-1$. The point is a vertex of the negative binary cube, so it must itself be one of the chosen bases. Each chosen $p$ is exposed. Take a linear functional with coefficient $-(n+1)$ in its negative coordinates and $1$ elsewhere. On the negative cube it is uniquely largest at $p$, and every nonnegative binary vertex has strictly smaller value. Thus the added fibers are exactly the assigned bodies. All continuous generators lie in $T$ and the core generator at each core base equals $T$. This proves the census and the hull is full dimensional.

Let $\lambda_i$ be the barycentric coordinates on $T$ and $b=1/(d+1)$. The $d+1$ caps $\lambda_i(x)-2\sum_j z_j\ge b$ capture all additions, the canonical own cap of volume $\Gamma_d V$, and none of the other core fibers. They cover the entire own fiber because the barycentric coordinates sum to one. At any other point of that fiber some $\lambda_i(x)>b$. Raising the corresponding cap threshold to this value strictly reduces the own volume and does not increase any other contribution. For a different core vertex $w$, the affine function
$$
(n+1)\sum_{i:w_i=1}(1-z_i)+\sum_{i:w_i=0}z_i
$$
vanishes at $w$ and is at least one at every other core vertex and every added base. At an added base it is at least $(n+1)|\operatorname{supp} w|-n\ge1$. Subtracting twice this function from each $\lambda_i(x)$ and taking threshold $b$ gives a cap cover of the $w$ fiber with mass $\Gamma_d V$. At an added base an exposed vertical cap has mass $|A_p|\le E$. The lower bound and these strict comparisons prove uniqueness on the full integer census. Divide by $2^nV+E$ and differentiate the resulting rational expression at zero for the final claim.

statement:
Let $n\ge1$, $d\ge2$, and let $T\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a $d$-simplex of volume $V$ and centroid $g$. Use $\Gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$ and the reflected simplex profile minimum $\rho_d$ from fact 53fe12b742a7608d. Let an actual compact convex source have fibers $T$ at all bases of $Q=\lbrace0,1\rbrace^n$. Suppose the positive-volume fibers outside $Q$ have bases $p\in[-1,2]^n\cap\mathbb Z^n\setminus Q$ and are bodies $A_p\subseteq T$. Define $q(p)$ by clipping the coordinates of $p$ to $[0,1]$, and put $E_q=\sum_{q(p)=q}|A_p|$. If $E_q\le\rho_d V$, the raw mixed closed-halfspace depth of $(q,g)$ is at least $\Gamma_d V+E_q$.

Conversely choose a nonempty subset of the shell bases having the same $q(p)=q$ and place any positive convex bodies $A_p\subseteq T$ there. The convex hull of these and the binary simplex fibers has exactly the assigned integer fibers. If their extra mass $E$ is at most $\rho_d V$, its unique maximizing mixed-integer point is $(q,g)$, with raw depth $\Gamma_d V+E$ and normalized depth $(\Gamma_d+E/V)/(2^n+E/V)$. In particular along $E=tW+o(t)$ the normalized right derivative at $t=0$ is $W(2^n-\Gamma_d)/(4^n V)$.
title: Aggregate credit and exact depth for small shell additions at one anchor
